title: BitLINK: Temporal Linkage of Address Clusters in Bitcoin Blockchain

problem.claim: An entity may control multiple distinct address clusters, creating a need to link disjoint clusters across time.

gap.claim: The abstract does not describe an existing method for linking address clusters when one cluster is abandoned and another is formed shortly thereafter.

contributions.claim: A deep neural network model links address clusters across time using synchronous actions derived from unlabeled data in a self-supervised manner.
The model assesses whether two clusters exhibit synchronous temporal signatures indicative of shared entity ownership.

narrative_sequence.summary: Entities such as gambling services may control multiple distinct Bitcoin address clusters.
Trust relationships between disjoint clusters can be established from abandonment and subsequent formation patterns.
The authors developed a self-supervised deep neural network using synchronous actions from unlabeled data.
The model evaluates synchronous temporal signatures as indicators of shared ownership.

source_observation.claim: Synchronous temporal actions can provide signals for linking otherwise disjoint address clusters.

interpretation.claim: Temporal coordination may serve as an ownership signal when direct labels or explicit links are unavailable.

application.claim: Use self-supervised temporal-signature models to investigate entity continuity across changing address clusters.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that synchronous signatures uniquely identify shared ownership.

unknowns: No empirical results, datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or performance numbers are reported.
The abstract does not specify the temporal window, model architecture, or operational definition of synchronous actions.
The abstract does not establish whether the inferred links are accurate or independently verified.
